title: Non-invertible Lattice 1-Form Symmetries for Non-Abelian Topological Order
authors: Rafael Flores-Calderón, Frank Pollmann, Michael Knap
abstract: Higher-form symmetries generalize conventional global symmetries and act on lower-dimensional submanifolds of a quantum system. While Abelian topological phases can be organized by 1-form symmetries that form a group, non-Abelian topological phases based on finite groups require 1-form symmetry operators governed by non-invertible fusion algebras. In this work, we make this statement precise in quantum double lattice models $\mathcal D(G)$ for finite non-Abelian groups $G$. We construct the electric, magnetic, and dyonic 1-form operators directly at the lattice fixed point and show that together they form a complete nonlocal diagnostic algebra for the topological Hilbert space. Using these operators, we explicitly determine the cylinder and torus ground-state subspaces for arbitrary finite $G$. Furthermore, we calculate the microscopic fusion and gluing of the 1-form symmetries and show that their topological deformation properties emerge after projection to the defect-free topological subspace. Our results establish ground states of non-Abelian quantum double models as a concrete microscopic realization of spontaneous non-invertible 1-form symmetry breaking and provide an operator language that may be useful for characterizing such states in quantum processors.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous framework to describe non-Abelian topological order using higher-form symmetries, specifically focusing on Kitaev quantum double lattice models. By constructing electric, magnetic, and dyonic 1-form operators, the authors provide an operator language that diagnoses the system's topological ground state degeneracy. This work offers a microscopic realization of spontaneous breaking of non-invertible symmetries.
main_problem: The work aims to precisely characterize non-Abelian topological order by understanding its underlying symmetry structure, specifically involving higher-form symmetries.
main_result: The paper establishes a concrete microscopic realization of spontaneous non-invertible 1-form symmetry breaking using quantum double lattice models. It provides an operator language for characterizing these complex topological states.
method: The authors construct electric, magnetic, and dyonic 1-form operators directly on the lattice fixed point to diagnose the topological Hilbert space structure.
model_or_system: The focus is on Kitaev quantum double lattice models $\mathcal D(G)$ for arbitrary finite non-Abelian groups $G$. The analysis builds upon understanding Abelian prototypes like the Z2 toric code.
key_observables: Electric Wilson loops ($W_{\Gamma}$), magnetic 't Hooft loops ($T_C$), and dyonic ribbon operators ($K_{CR}$); these form a complete nonlocal diagnostic algebra.
important_parameters: The structure depends on the finite non-Abelian group $G$ and its representations $	ext{Rep}(G)$ and conjugacy classes $	ext{Class}(G)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that projecting microscopic lattice operators onto the defect-free topological subspace recovers the expected continuum fusion rules.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates non-invertible higher-form symmetries using string-net pictures on a torus for $D(G)$, labeling the key diagnostic operators. Table I shows eigenvalues for the Z2 toric code ground states.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from reviewing Abelian prototypes (like the toric code) to defining the necessary non-invertible 1-form symmetry operators for general finite groups $G$. It then constructs these operators on the lattice and derives the resulting topological degeneracy and fusion rules, culminating in a microscopic understanding of spontaneous symmetry breaking.
why_interesting: The explicit construction of diagnostic operators for non-Abelian order provides a powerful theoretical tool to characterize exotic quantum phases that are relevant for fault-tolerant quantum computation architectures based on anyons.
